status: Shore foam detail correction. Procedural surface shading; not breaking-surf simulation or proof of photorealistic production readiness.
changes: Replace broad soft noise with a generated 1024 x 1024 seamless texture containing rounded pores of varying sizes, microfroth and macro breakup.
Two world-space drifting layers; four-metre base tile (~3.9 mm texels), mipmaps and up to 8x anisotropic filtering.
Millimetre-scale normal relief and foam-dependent roughness respond to scene lighting.
One RGBA8 texture per prepared water state, shared across its ocean and local bodies (~5.3 MiB including mipmaps); immutable CPU bytes cached after first generation.
GPU texture upload and validation occur before document/history commit; failed allocations dispose candidate resources and retain existing water.

validation.build: npm run build passed (strict types, runtime/declarations, editor).
validation.lint: npm run lint and changed-file Prettier checks passed.
validation.browser: Five scenarios passed: water-foam (1), water authoring/recovery (2), water-lighting (1), temporal-aa (1). Full browser suite not rerun.

validation.recovery: Injected RGBA8 1024 x 1024 foam allocation failure as well as existing height/shore failures; previous document, redo and visibility retained; retry and undo/redo passed.
validation.visual: Inspected before/after close-up, oblique and temporal fixture screenshots. Initial polygonal cellular detail was revised to rounded, differently sized pores and patch breakup.
validation.fixture: 1280 x 720 built-runtime planar beach, six-metre orthographic close-up, real lighting/refraction; metric measures two-pixel (~9 mm) variation in the foam-minus-plain image, not a photorealism score.

performance.interpretation: Water-enabled GPU medians changed from 9.40/9.61 to 10.02/10.03 ms; FPS changed from 57.1/57.7 to 55.6/52.7. The water-off control also varied (8.94 to 9.76 ms GPU, 58.7 to 50.4 FPS), so these sequential runs do not isolate the exact foam cost.
limits: Static camera, short measurement, background/clock/thermal variability.
The external coastal view is dominated by the finite terrain boundary and has little foam; it checks integration/overall water rendering cost, not a worst-case foam-covered screen.
No cross-device audit, whole-forest FPS guarantee, physical input latency measurement or long-session memory soak.
